transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because I've been dealing with some really strange thoughts and beliefs that others say aren't real, and it's been going on for over a year. My mood has also been swinging wildly between intense, hyperactive highs and deep, empty lows. It has just become too overwhelming to handle on my own.
Do these strange thoughts and beliefs only happen when you are feeling very high or very low, or do they also occur when your mood is relatively stable and normal?

Yes, they actually do happen even when my mood is relatively stable and normal. There was a period of about two or three weeks where my emotions felt completely fine, but those strange thoughts and beliefs were still very much there. They don't seem to go away just because my mood evens out.
When you experience these intense, hyperactive highs, how long do they typically last, and do they cause major disruptions in your daily life?

These high-energy periods typically last for about three weeks at a time. They cause major disruptions in my life because I end up going on reckless buying sprees, spending excessive amounts of money, and making rash business investments without really looking into them. It has ended up causing me a lot of financial distress.
During those times when your mood is stable and normal, do you also experience other unusual things, such as hearing voices or seeing things that others cannot?

Yes, I do. Even when my mood is completely stable and normal, I still hear voices and see things that aren't actually there. That has happened for at least two weeks at a time during those calm periods.

latest_inference.note: The patient meets the criteria for Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type) because they experience active psychotic symptoms (delusions and hallucinations) for at least 2-3 weeks in the absence of a major mood episode, alongside a history of manic episodes (hyperactive highs lasting 3 weeks with reckless behavior and financial distress) and depressive episodes. This rules out Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features, where psychosis only occurs during mood episodes.
